canonical_title: The Book of Philip K. Dick
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: An early paperback story collection (published 1973, also known as The Turning Wheel) that gathers Dick's 1950s magazine tales of suburban unease, robots, and reality coming loose at the seams.
page_summary:
The Book of Philip K. Dick is a 1973 paperback collection of stories drawn from Dick's prolific 1950s output for the science-fiction magazines. It circulated under more than one title over its printing history and belongs to the wave of anthologies that kept his short fiction in print between his novels.

The stories reflect the concerns of that period: the tidy postwar suburb turned strange, the robot or automaton that raises questions about what its makers owe it, and the ordinary person who discovers the everyday world is a facade over something else. These are compact, premise-driven tales, the workshop in which Dick tested ideas he would later expand into novels.

As a collection, it matters less for a single famous title than for showing Dick's short-story instincts at work across a range of registers, from comic to paranoid, all circling the recurring suspicion that reality is provisional.
